% ---------------------------------------------------------------- Table: variants
\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\caption{What each model in the result tables is. \emph{Retrained}: epochs of training after compression (recipe in Table~\ref{tab:setup}).}
\label{tab:variants}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.18}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.5cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.1cm}L>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{1.45cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{What changes} & \textbf{Settings} & \makecell{\textbf{Re-}\\\textbf{trained}} \\
\midrule
FP32 baseline & ResNet-18 trained on HAM10000 (Table~\ref{tab:setup}). The reference for every comparison. & 11.18\,M parameters, 3.64 GFLOPs & -- \\
FP32 control & The baseline fine-tuned for \textbf{10 more epochs} with exactly the pruning recipe, \textbf{without} any compression. & Not a compression method. Extra training alone changes the scores, so a pruned model should also be compared with the control: pruned $-$ control = effect of pruning only. & 10 ep. \\
\addlinespace[2pt]\multicolumn{4}{@{}l}{\textit{Quantization}} \\
Weight-only PTQ & Conv and \texttt{fc} weights stored as INT8, turned back into FP32 when loaded. & Symmetric, scale $=\max|w|/127$, one scale per tensor or per output channel. Only the file shrinks: compute stays FP32. & No \\
Static PTQ (W8A8) & Weights \emph{and} activations in INT8, integer kernels. & x86 backend; weights per-channel symmetric, activations per-tensor affine; ranges calibrated on 1{,}000 class-stratified training images (3 different sets tried). & No \\
QAT (W8A8) & Same INT8 format as static PTQ, but trained with simulated quantization. & Starts from the static-PTQ ranges (Table~\ref{tab:setup}). & 10 ep. \\
\addlinespace[2pt]\multicolumn{4}{@{}l}{\textit{Pruning}} \\
Unstructured pruning & Individual weights set to zero; layer shapes unchanged. & Global L1 magnitude over all conv and \texttt{fc} weights; 30/50/70/90\% zeroed. Mask kept during fine-tuning. Zeros are still stored and computed (dense kernels). & 10 ep. \\
Filter pruning & Whole convolution filters removed: thinner layers. & L1 norm of each filter; same ratio (10/20/30/40\%) in every channel group (Torch-Pruning dependency graph); stem \texttt{conv1} and \texttt{fc} untouched. & 10 ep. \\
Block pruning & Whole residual blocks replaced by identity: shallower network. & Removed in a greedy order: \texttt{layer2.1}, \texttt{layer1.0}, \texttt{layer3.1}, \texttt{layer4.1}, \texttt{layer1.1} (1 to 5 blocks); BatchNorm re-estimated on 2{,}000 training images before fine-tuning. & 10 ep. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\scriptsize
\item \textit{How to read.} Bal.\ Acc.\ = macro recall; Mel.\ Rec.\ = melanoma recall. 95\% CIs are about $\pm$4 points on macro F1, so 1--2 point differences without $^{\ast}$ are not meaningful. For averaged rows ($^{\dagger}$), $^{\ast}$ means significant in all 3 runs in the same direction; per-run spread is in Table~\ref{tab:seed-robustness}. Static PTQ efficiency is measured on the seed-42 model (the 3 calibrations give the same architecture).
\item \textit{Speed.} Lat.: batch 1, median of 200 runs (30 warm-up), median of 3 interleaved repeats, at 1 thread (1T) and 4 threads (4T). Thr.: batch 32. Peak RAM: memory increase while loading and warming up. GFLOPs are counted on the FP32 graph for every model (INT8 runs the same operations in INT8). Models were timed in 4 sessions and FP32 latency varied from 50.7 to 54.0\,ms between them, so speed-up and $\Delta$Energy are computed against the FP32 model timed in the same session: compare those rather than absolute latencies.
\item \textit{Environment.} Per 1{,}000 images at 1 thread. Energy is a CodeCarbon estimate (no hardware power counter; about 250\,W per active thread assumed), so it follows run time; differences below about 5\% are noise. CO$_2$e: Tunisian grid, 564\,g\,CO$_2$e/kWh.
\item[a] Weights are INT8 on disk only; they are converted back to FP32 when loaded, so speed and energy do not change (by design).
\item[b] Zeros are still stored and computed, hence no gain in size or speed. Non-zero parameters: 7.83/5.59/3.36/1.13\,M; gzip-compressed file: 32.0/24.3/16.2/7.2\,MB (FP32: 41.6\,MB).
\item[] Pruned models and the control keep the fine-tuning epoch with the best validation macro F1, so their scores are slightly optimistic. The test split has not been used.
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}
\end{sidewaystable}
